exposure: uterine incision-to-delivery interval (<120 seconds, 121-239 seconds, >=240 seconds)
outcome: composite neonatal adverse outcomes (respiratory support, therapeutic hypothermia, birth injury, neonatal death)
cohort: The study included 5,850 singleton pregnancies delivered by non-urgent cesarean delivery at term (>=37 weeks) in a single tertiary medical center between 2017-2021, excluding cases with fetal/maternal compromise, major fetal anomalies, fetal death, or missing data.
finding: Longer uterine incision-to-delivery intervals in non-urgent term cesarean deliveries were independently associated with increased risk of neonatal morbidity, as well as acidemia.
mod_finding: Longer uterine incision-to-delivery intervals during non-urgent term cesarean deliveries were independently associated with increased risk of neonatal morbidity and acidemia.
